Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:180273
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 38256 of 2023

Applicant :- Vivek
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Vashistha
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Rajeev Dhar Dwivedi, learned AGA, for the State, apprised the Court that on 17.8.2023 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
2. Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Ajay Kumar Vashistha, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajeev Dhar Dwivedi,
learned AGA, for the State.
4.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.31 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366 and 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Malawan, District Etah during pendency of the trial.
5. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and according to the FIR, applicant enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 16 years.

sentences.text:
6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation of enticement made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and although victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. stated that she had gone along with applicant and her one another friend and with her consent applicant made physical relationship with her but when her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded then she changed her earlier version given under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and stated that in anger she had left her paternal home and went at the house of her 'Bua' and she categorically stated that applicant had not taken her.
7.
He further submits that during trial prosecutrix of the case, i.e., daughter of the informant has been declared hostile as she did not support the prosecution case.
8. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 6.3.2023.
9. Per contra, learned AGA although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Considering the fact that prosecutrix of the case neither in her statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. nor in her statement recorded by trial court made any allegation against the applicant, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant-Vivek be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the Vivek vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153631221/
2 merits of the case during trial.
